change.reason: Merge the remaining general peak-readiness details into the existing foresight and 5% supply-reserve policy. Preserve advance inventory funding and separately planned wafer, tool and supplier protections; do not retain a redundant dated peak-readiness event.

before.statement: Adam used knowledge of the original timeline to identify investment opportunities and anticipate emerging demand. As his companies changed markets, he combined that knowledge with contemporary research, customer evidence and production planning. His public explanation was disciplined data analysis; the origin of his advantage remained secret. Throughout the story, Adam uses his foresight to anticipate demand and always maintains supply capacity at forecast demand plus 5%, keeping that reserve available to respond to demand. This is good-output supply headroom, not an increase in forecast sales or a requirement to hold permanent excess stock. Equipment utilisation and protection against a failed production tool are planned separately.

after.statement: Adam used knowledge of the original timeline to identify investment opportunities and anticipate emerging demand. His public explanation was disciplined data analysis; the origin of his advantage remained secret. Throughout the story, Adam uses his foresight to anticipate demand and always maintains supply capacity at forecast demand plus 5%, keeping that reserve available to respond to demand. This is good-output supply headroom, not an increase in forecast sales or a requirement to hold permanent excess stock. Wafer supply, tool redundancy and supplier lead times are planned and funded as separate protections.
